messages.subject: [R-GSoC] Next Steps
parts:
Student Applications are now closed. I believe R received more high
quality applications this year than in any previous year. Some
projects received as many as 6 applications, so this will be a
competitive and difficult year to choose winners.

Thank you all for participating.

Now to go over next steps. Both Students and Mentors have things to
do. Failure to complete these tasks will result in not getting a slot.

Students:
You may not, under any circumstances, ask about whether you have been
accepted, or are likely to be accepted to GSoC this year. Google will
inform all of the thousands of students who applied to GSoC at the same
time, and announce those who have slots on the GSoC website.

Google will be reviewing your proof of enrollment. In many cases, they
will be asking you to update it to provide proof of current enrollment
or other eligibility issues for GSoC. Pay close attention to these
requests, and respond as quickly as possible. Google does not share
these requests with org admins (Toby and me) or Mentors. If you do not
have updated or accepted final proof or enrollment on file by Google's
deadline (I believe Apr 15th), you will not be eligible to receive a
slot.

Mentors:
Some mentors have not accepted their invitations.  If you're having
trouble, please contact Toby or me immediately, and we'll try to help
you.  If we do not have all listed mentors in the Google system by slot
assignment time, with feedback entered as below, your project idea will
not get a slot.

You must not communicate with students about acceptance or rejection.
Nothing is Final till May and the Google announcement.

Toby and I will be doing a first review of submitted applications.  We
will be commenting on proposals and contacting mentors individually for
feedback where necessary.  According to Google guidelines, discussion
about student proposals should happen in the comment section of the
proposal wherever possible (Students don't see this section).

We also need all R Project Mentors to do a few things on the Google
Summer of Code system as soon as possible:

1> We need you to select 'Want to Mentor' on an application for a
project where you are listed as a mentor, or on the strongest
application for the project where there are multiple applications for a
single project.  

2> We also need you to comment on *all* applications for projects where
you are listed as a mentor in the 'Comment on this Proposal' section at
the bottom of the proposal page.  Please provide a succinct summary of
your feelings on the application.  These comments are visible to other
R mentors only, not to the students.  We want all mentors to comment on
all proposals for a project you are a listed mentor for.

3> We *want*, but cannot require, that you comment on other student
applications for proposed projects that you will not be mentoring this
summer.  Please comment on projects where you have some expertise.
Google used to require all mentors to vote on applications, but that
was removed from the process last year.  Your input is still very
valuable to Toby and me as we review applications and make slot
requests.

Slot request to Google will happen no later than April 17th, per the
Google Deadline.  You will see slot request numbers start to show up as
early as today, and preliminary starring of high quality proposals.
None of these are final. Feel free to contact Toby and me off-list
with questions or concerns. Input on applications should go in the
'Comment on This Proposal' section, as described above. 

April 19th-24th Toby and I will communicate with mentors and allocate
the slots we've received from Google.  

On May 4th, accepted projects will be announced by Google.

Between April 3rd and May 4th, Google prohibits mentors and
organizations from telling students whether or not their proposal has
been accepted.  Students, please don't ask.  Mentors, you must not
tell.  Google takes a very dim view of breaking this rule.

As always, please do not hesitate to contact me or Toby with any
questions or concerns.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
